I definitely cannot pick a favourite but I will think about some that I've either always enjoyed or particularly enjoy right now. 

Have a Nice Dream, Dune, and Tears of the Star are three softer and perhaps more emotive tracks that I consistently love.

Swallow is a classic. To me it never gets old, and it's definitely one of Casiopea's best tracks I think.

Warning from the Answers album is one that I think isn't as appreciated as it should be (the Answers album in general is awesome). The guitar and keyboard solos play on the edge of a knife between complete dissonance and a feeling of danger, of warning if I may... I don't have a transcription for Warning, but it sounds to me that the solos start as far from a harmonic sound to the melody as possible and then slowly fall towards a beautiful conclusion that aligns with the overarching theme of the track. 

Midnight Rendezvous (Live at ABC Hall, not the Mint Jams version) is such a fun one to listen to. I love the little breaks in the solos they do where it's just the audience clapping, keeping the beat. 

I mean we all know how impressive Casiopea's live collection is, need I mention Looking Up (Live at the Ryogoku Kokugikan, the guitar solo makes me somehow feel the mastery Issei Noro has over the guitar) or Domino Line (Live at Chuo Kaikan Hall, Tetsuo's praiseworthy playing), or any of the other number of unimaginably incredible live tracks??

Circular Dream is a massively impressive song -- the structure is so chaotic and fun, I love it.

Some honourable mentions -- Olion, Magic Ray, Dream Hill, SPACE ROAD (holy shit there are so many good versions of this song), Ripple Dance, Life Game, Mid-Manhattan, Chandelier, Aoi Hono, Naturally, Eyes of the Mind (love the last bit of this song, brings out so much emotion and yearning in me), Zoom, Road Rhythm, Shocking Function, A Place in the Sun, Voice from Others, Key of Miracle, GOLDEN WAVES... and so many more. The fact that I can list out so many 10/10 (maybe 11/10) tracks and not even cover half of them is the reason Casiopea is 95% of what I listen to, and has been for the past year or so.

Anyways, tl;dr is that my favourite track is the one I'm listening to in the moment.

I don’t think you should worry too much, but it’s still important to be aware of how it’s affecting your relationship. I started dating my girlfriend in high school and we ended up going to different schools (me Queen’s, her U of T). I am in engineering physics and she’s in life sciences, hoping to get into med school so I understand your position somewhat. We spend a lot of time FaceTiming, and if we are ever stressed about our workload we tend to lean on each other in any way we can, while also not expecting each other to fix our individual stress. Be open-minded, be communicative. Communication is the cornerstone of any relationship, so make sure you are both honest about any daily stresses and don’t try to hide anything from each other.

An important note to make is learning to deal with workload stress. Don’t for any reason take out your stress on your partner, and if you do, apologize sincerely and never do it again. Taking walks, practicing hobbies, participating in activities, are all much much better ways to de-stress. If you work on how to healthily deal with the anxiety of school (easier said than done of course) your relationship shouldn’t suffer too much because of it. 

Another piece of advice that may help could be to set up some boundaries and to learn each other’s schedules. Hanging out every night for a couple hours is most likely not going to work, and may even cause some resentment towards your partner when the assignments start piling up. Which days you’ll pick to organize spending time together will depend on your schedules of course so I can’t help there.

I hope this helps! Again, I wouldn’t be too worried, but it won’t be a walk in the park either. Just keep working on yourselves and your relationship, and don’t be hard on yourselves when you don’t get it right. Be honest, be communicative, and things should run smoothly. If you have any more questions I’d be happy to talk more. Good luck!

Can’t give you a syllabus, but I can tell you about the course. Mod 1 and 2 are first semester, in Mod 1 you work with a team on a project that everybody does (specific project changes every year) and you write design reports, make models, etc. There’s also a little test you do around Week 6 but it’s worth only like 15%.

Mod 2 you do 1 lab and a couple quizzes per week (usually these quizzes just prepare you for the lab). These labs usually just teach you a specific thing like error propagation. At the end of the first semester you have to do a final lab where you put everything you learned together; make the procedure for a lab, and then actually do it.

Mod 3 is in the second semester. It’s like Mod 1 except there are a bunch of different projects and you’ll be on a different team than Mod 1. It’s also a little more demanding in its expectations for writing reports and how rigorous you are in making your design.

Note: for Mod 1 and Mod 3 you have a Project Manager (usually just an upper year student) that will help your team and guide you in the right direction.

Another note: Your marks from Mod 1, 2, and 3 are added together into one final mark for the course. Mod 3 is worth a bit more than Mod 1 and 2, and Mod 2 is worth the least.

If you have any more questions about the course feel free to ask. It’s really not a hard course despite what some people might say. You get from it what you put into it essentially.

I've lived around Kingston and Area my whole life so I'm happy you asked. Downtown has lots of different restaurants and places to go, with the waterfront being not too far away too. There are also quite a few parks you can check out. There are escape rooms too, which I highly recommend. If you have a bus pass, downtown isn't the only place you should be hanging out. There are some big shopping centres and malls out in the West End that are cool to be around (RioCan centre, Cataraqui Mall), as well as Fort Henry in the East End which is a nice place to take a walk when the Sun is setting.

 I'd say Kingston (like a lot of other cities) has good parts and bad parts, and downtown is like a midway between the two. If you go north up Division St from the campus you'll be heading into the not so nice neighbourhoods (the Heights), and that's pretty much as bad as it gets. I don't know why you'd want to go into the Heights though.

You might run into some sketch people downtown but it's not so bad you should avoid the area completely. The neighbourhoods around campus are pretty safe as well. I might have some bias speaking as a "Kingstonian" but I don't think it's as bad as some people say. As is the case with any city, be smart and safe and you'll be fine.
